transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Kim (Redwood SE), Ravi Desai (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Peregrine SRE), Marcus Hale (Peregrine VP Eng), Priya Nair (Peregrine Security), Ethan Wu (Peregrine Platform), Samir Rao (Peregrine Infra)

Summary: quick RCA walkthrough of the 2026-10-18 dispatch latency spike, alignment on mitigations (cache fixes, autoscaler tuning), security/compliance gating for pilot, and next steps for a dedicated capacity pilot.

Topics: RCA timeline, KV cache behaviour, autoscaler/fallback interaction, canary + rollback plan, SOC2/KMS questions, pilot SOW and pricing.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this focused. Today is an RCA + remediation kickoff following the spike on the 18th. Lena, can you start with what you saw?
[00:27] Lena (Peregrine): Sure, uh, thanks. So on the 18th between 14:12 and 14:37 UTC we saw sustained request latencies go from our baseline ~150ms p95 to something like 1.8 to 2.2 seconds, tokens soared, and we had a small amount of fallback to smaller model variants which made things worse. We also saw worker churn — GPU pods restarted a few times with OOM-ish traces.
[01:05] Marcus (Peregrine): To add, peak dispatch volume was about 2.7x normal because of a promo — so the traffic profile changed quickly. The problem is that our SLAs for dispatch contain hard 300ms targets for the UI.
[01:42] Jonas (Redwood): Got it. On our side we looked at traces and the initial signal was a KV cache growth in the prefix cache — lots of slightly different prompts, prefix keys not coalescing, so the KV store grew and pushed memory pressure. When the runtime saw that pressure, autoscaler attempted to spin up more instances but there was a brief scheduling window where a mix of old and new kernels caused mismatched placement and then fallback to a smaller model variant happened which increased per-request latency and token count.
[02:25] Ethan (Peregrine): Wait, fallback — was that because of model mismatch or because of timeouts? We saw some 504-ish things in our logs.
[02:40] Jonas (Redwood): It's a combination. The runtime's fallback policy kicks in when memory errors or slow startup are detected; it routes to a 'compatible' model with smaller memory footprint. That's why tokens spiked — the variant had different tokenization and more conservative decoding settings, so more tokens per user request.
[03:12] Speaker 2: so, um, the K V cache — is that persisted or ephemeral? Because if it's surviving across restarts it's going to bloat.
[03:30] Jonas (Redwood): Good point. The prefix/KV cache is in-memory on the worker (not persisted to disk). But there's an eviction policy; what we observed is eviction didn't trigger fast enough because keys kept being touched with slightly different prefixes, so TTL heuristics failed to reclaim. Also, GC pressure + a regression in a kernel change from last release made the memory usage path denser.
[04:05] Samir (Peregrine): We observed a corresponding increase in GPU memory used per pod right before the restarts, then the pods restarted and the autoscaler started creating more pods but because of scheduling exhaustion the new pods ended up in a different AZ with slightly different GPU drivers — a mismatch — and the runtime didn't like that.
[04:45] Priya (Peregrine Security): Quick security question — during that time did any logs with PII get preserved in our logs or in Redwood traces? We need to be sure no sensitive data left encryption boundaries.
[05:02] Jonas (Redwood): Short answer — no evidence of PII being written to persistent logs. The runtime redacts prompt metadata before sending to logs in prod, and we also have customer-configurable KMS encryption at rest. We'll provide the exact audit entries.
[05:22] Lena (Peregrine): We pulled a sample and saw no PII in the logs, but there were more debug level traces stored in the short-term bucket due to elevated logging during the spike window. We'll share that subset.
[05:45] Maya (Redwood): Okay, I'll make a note to include the audit log slice in the packet.

--- Action recap (spoken live) ---
[06:10] Maya (Redwood): High level RCA path from Redwood: 1) prefix/KV cache growth + eviction heuristic mismatch, 2) runtime kernel regression increased per-model memory, 3) autoscaler scheduling jitter across AZs, 4) fallback routing to smaller variant which increased tokenization and latency. For remediation: immediate mitigations, medium-term fixes, and pilot options.

[06:45] Marcus (Peregrine): Immediate means what? We have customers impacted.
[06:52] Jonas (Redwood): Immediate mitigations we suggested earlier are: reduce cache TTL aggressively for the next 48 hours, disable the newest kernel patch in the Canary group, and pin the model variant so fallback doesn't trigger while we're stabilizing. We can also temporarily increase reserved capacity for your peak windows.
[07:20] Lena (Peregrine): The TTL change — will that drop accuracy or increase token counts?
[07:33] Jonas (Redwood): Some downside — cold-start tokens for some prefixes may increase briefly, but it should reduce sustained memory growth and avoid OOMs. Tradeoff is small compared to multi-second latencies.

[08:05] Speaker 3 (Ravi): A couple of commercial notes — if Peregrine is interested in a Dedicated pilot, that gives you pinned pools and reduced noisy neighbour risk and more predictable scheduling across AZs. Maya, can you speak to timing?
[08:22] Maya (Redwood): Yes, we have a 1-week pilot option for Dedicated where we allocate a small reserved pool and run load across your normal traffic. Pricing will be in a tiered packet; we'll send details after this call. It will also let you do a controlled canary without cross-tenant scheduler jitter.
[08:48] Priya (Peregrine): For compliance, we need to validate KMS integrations and that audit logs meet our retention. Also need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC mapping for our SOC2 auditors.
[09:05] Maya (Redwood): We have a security checklist and SOC2 artifacts — I'll include them. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and SAML for SSO.

[09:30] Lena (Peregrine): Can we talk timeline for the immediate mitigations? We need them before the next promo window.
[09:38] Jonas (Redwood): We can push TTL heuristic changes in 2 hours as a hotfix toggle; kernel rollback for the canary will need coordination — 24 to 48 hours to stage and verify depending on Canary window. Pinning fallback policy is a config change and we can flip it in ~30 minutes, but we'd like to do that in a maintenance window so we can monitor.

[10:15] Ethan (Peregrine): On the scheduler az mismatch — will Dedicated fix that outright?
[10:22] Jonas (Redwood): Dedicated significantly reduces that risk because nodes are reserved for your tenancy and we can ensure uniform kernel/drivers across the pool. For Hosted, we still do our best, but cloud scheduling and transient capacity events can cause heterogeneity.

[10:50] Marcus (Peregrine): Any quick wins on monitoring/alerts so we detect KV growth before it becomes a problem?
[10:59] Jonas (Redwood): Yep — we can add an eviction headroom metric and an alert when KV keycount growth rate exceeds X% over a rolling minute, and also an early-warning for swap/GPU memory deltas. We'll propose thresholds based on your normal profile.

[11:25] Speaker 2: uh, will that require agent changes on our side?
[11:32] Jonas (Redwood): No, those are runtime metrics we can surface to your dashboard; you'll get alert hooks for PagerDuty/Slack. If you want client-side sampling we can add traces but it's optional.

[12:00] Priya (Peregrine): About the logs and PII again — what's the retention window for the short-term diagnostic bucket? We need to ensure that any debug artifacts are under our retention policy.
[12:15] Maya (Redwood): Standard debug retention is 30 days for the short-term bucket, but for Private deployments you can set that. We'll include the retention config in the security packet.

[12:50] Lena (Peregrine): We're also worried about the fallback variant's tokenization model differences — any way to force identical tokenization?
[13:05] Jonas (Redwood): We can avoid fallback by pinning and we also have 'tokenization parity' checks when creating compatible variants; we'll run a quick consistency diff for the top 200 prompt templates you provided. That will tell us if the variant will blow up token counts.

[13:42] Marcus (Peregrine): On the timeline: we need the hotfix TTL change in next 48 hours; a kernel rollback can be staged in 24–48; a pilot for Dedicated before the next promo in three weeks.
[13:58] Maya (Redwood): Sounds doable. We'll prioritize the TTL hotfix and pin fallback for the immediate window.

[14:20] Speaker 4 (Samir): One more infra note — our cluster clouds have node anti-affinity rules, is that something Redwood can respect for scheduled pods?
[14:35] Jonas (Redwood): We can adopt placement constraints as part of a Dedicated pool and for Private deployments. For Hosted it's limited by provider-side scheduling. We'll document the options.

[15:05] Maya (Redwood): Ok we'll move into the remediation plan doc. Jonas, can you outline short-term, medium-term, and long-term items?
[15:15] Jonas (Redwood): Short-term (48h): reduce KV cache TTL, pin fallback, add early-warning alerts. Medium-term (2–4 weeks): kernel regression rollback in canary, protection for the eviction heuristics, and improved model variant parity checks. Long-term (1–3 months): autoscaler improvements, smarter placement to avoid cross-AZ drift, and a dedicated capacity program if you opt in.

[16:02] Lena (Peregrine): For the medium-term, will the kernel rollback require a full model reload, or is it a runtime patch?
[16:12] Jonas (Redwood): It's a runtime kernel roll back — it requires restarting the workers in the canary group and reloading model weights but we can orchestrate warm-up to avoid cold-start latency. We'll coordinate the window.

[16:40] Marcus (Peregrine): Regarding the dedicated pilot — what telemetry will we get access to? Raw metrics, token-level cost breakdowns?
[16:52] Maya (Redwood): You'll get the full Console access: per-route token/latency breakdowns, per-model tracing, and the ability to set alert thresholds. We'll also grant a restricted SSO role to your SREs.

[17:18] Priya (Peregrine): KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys across Hosted and Dedicated?
[17:27] Jonas (Redwood): We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and for Dedicated we can support it in most regions; Hosted has provider constraints in a few cloud regions but for your region we can enable customer KMS. We'll include region-specific notes.

[18:00] Speaker 3 (Ravi): Ok, let's capture the immediate playbook: TTL toggle (Jonas), pin fallback (Maya+Jonas), alerts (Jonas), SOW/pricing (Maya), and security packet (Maya + security team). We'll list owners in the doc and send it out.

[18:32] Lena (Peregrine): We'll share the promo schedule and traffic windows so you can align the pilot.
[18:40] Marcus (Peregrine): Also include a small bench of 30k tokens/sec test we can run on the pilot to verify under load.

[19:05] Jonas (Redwood): We'll propose a test harness. It will simulate your template distribution and include the top 50 prompt templates.

[19:40] Maya (Redwood): Anything else on compliance? Priya?
[19:46] Priya (Peregrine): We also need to confirm whether audit logs are immutable for the period our compliance team requires. If not immutable we need a mitigation plan.
[20:00] Maya (Redwood): We'll include retention and immutability options; for Dedicated and Private we can provide stronger immutability guarantees.

[20:30] Speaker 2: I'm seeing a question in chat about whether the prefix cache can be sharded by tenant key to reduce cross-key blow-up.
[20:42] Jonas (Redwood): Yes, sharding the prefix key space by tenant and adding a per-tenant cap is on our roadmap and is a medium-term mitigation. We can expedite it if you sign up for pilot capacity since it's higher priority.

[21:10] Lena (Peregrine): We'll consider that. Quick request — capture the exact config changes you'll make for TTL and fallback so we can mirror them in our staging tests.
[21:20] Jonas (Redwood): Sure — I'll post a config diff and the runbook with exact toggles.

[22:00] Maya (Redwood): Ok, let's do a quick verbal recap of next steps and owners.
[22:10] Maya (Redwood): Jonas — gather heap profiles and KV dumps, add alerts, propose TTL value.
[22:18] Jonas (Redwood): Yep.
[22:20] Maya (Redwood): Lena — share the request IDs and promo schedule.
[22:25] Lena (Peregrine): Will do.
[22:28] Maya (Redwood): Priya — compile compliance blockers.
[22:30] Priya (Peregrine): On it.
[22:32] Maya (Redwood): Ravi — prepare canary runbook and coordinate internal dry-run.
[22:35] Ravi (Redwood): Yup.

[23:00] Marcus (Peregrine): Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[23:05] Maya (Redwood): Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and the SOW draft.
